BUG REPORT (from a user):
Wrapping one of the library's error values (not a pointer) with fmt.Errorf and then trying to match the original error through it fails:

    err := Error{Err: innerErr, Type: ErrorTypeAny}
    wrapped := fmt.Errorf("wrapped: %w", err)
    errors.Is(wrapped, innerErr) // false, expected true
    var target TestErr
    errors.As(wrapped, &target)  // false, expected true

The same code works when wrapping a pointer to the error instead, so the value form should behave identically.

LIKELY CAUSE (verify it yourself, do not assume): in /gin/errors.go, `func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error` has a pointer receiver, while `func (msg Error) Error() string` has a value receiver. So a gin.Error *value* stored inside a fmt.Errorf wrap chain does not implement `interface{ Unwrap() error }` and errors.Is/errors.As cannot traverse into it. The doc comment on Unwrap says it exists "to allow interoperability with errors.Is(), errors.As() and errors.Unwrap()".

TASK:
1. Read /gin/errors.go and confirm the root cause. Also check whether other methods on Error have receiver inconsistencies that break the documented contract (e.g. methods needed for error/Unwrap interfaces). Only fix what is a genuine, repository-evident bug; keep the change minimal.
2. Apply the minimal fix (most likely changing Unwrap to a value receiver `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error`), making sure both value `Error` and pointer `*Error` forms work with errors.Is/errors.As.
3. Verify with a temporary standalone Go test/program OUTSIDE the repo test files (e.g. write a small program in /tmp that imports the module via a replace directive, or use `go run` in a temp dir) reproducing the user's snippet for BOTH the value and pointer forms, and confirm both now return true. Delete any temporary files you created outside /tmp afterwards; do not leave stray files in /gin.
4. Run the repository's pre-existing test suite: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./...` (and `go vet ./...`). Confirm no pre-existing test regresses. Note: the repo may have some tests that need network or are slow; report any failures with the exact test name and whether they also fail before your change (you can check with `git stash`).
5. Report back concisely: root cause, exact diff applied, the commands you ran, their results, and confirmation that no pre-existing test regressed.

BUG REPORT (from a user):
I set the status to 200 and flushed the response, then later code tried to set it to 401. I expected the original 200 to remain because the response had already been sent, but calling Status() afterward returned 401. The client still received 200, so my logs and metrics now report a status that was never actually sent.

    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
    w.WriteHeaderNow()

    // later, after the response is already sent
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusUnauthorized)
    fmt.Println(w.Status()) // got 401, expected 200

TASK:
1. Read /gin/response_writer.go carefully (and /gin/context.go usage of the writer). Identify the root cause: likely `WriteHeader` unconditionally assigns `w.status = code` even when the response has already been written (`w.Written()` / `w.size != noWritten`), whereas `WriteHeaderNow` and `Write` correctly ignore later status changes. Confirm by reading the code; do not assume.
2. Check the documented contract in the repo: doc comments on ResponseWriter methods, README/CHANGELOG, and any other in-repo statement about status semantics (e.g. that the first WriteHeader wins / that a status cannot be changed after the response is written). The fix must be justified by in-repo evidence, not by your own preference.
3. IMPORTANT: before editing, run the pre-existing tests and record the baseline: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. Then check /gin/response_writer_test.go and any other tests that exercise WriteHeader/Status to make sure your fix does not break a pre-existing green test. If a pre-existing test asserts the current (buggy) behavior, DO NOT change that test; in that case report the conflict to me instead of making the change.
4. Apply the minimal fix so that WriteHeader does not overwrite the status once the response has already been written (i.e. status is only set on the first WriteHeader, matching WriteHeaderNow/Write behavior). Keep the change minimal and idiomatic.
5. Verify: write a temporary standalone reproduction OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/repro2 with a go.mod using `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`, GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off) that runs a gin engine with httptest and reproduces the user's sequence, asserting Status()==200 after the late WriteHeader(401) and that the client receives 200. Also test the normal case: WriteHeader(401) then Status()==401 and client sees 401. Clean up /tmp files when done; leave no stray files in /gin.
6. Run `cd /gin && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...`. Confirm no pre-existing test regresses (compare with the baseline from step 3; you can also `git stash` to double-check).
7. Report back concisely: root cause, exact diff, commands run and results, and confirmation that no pre-existing test regressed (or the conflict if there is one).

BUG REPORT (from a user):
I'm serving a download whose filename comes from user input, and the quotes and backslashes in it end up in the response header exactly as I passed them:

    c.FileAttachment("./report.pdf", `evil"; dummy="x.sh`)

I expected the filename to be escaped so the header still contains a single, well-formed filename, but instead the raw quotes and backslashes are written straight through, producing something like `attachment; filename="evil"; dummy="x.sh"`. Any client or intermediary reading that header sees extra parameters I never set, which is a real problem when the filename isn't fully under my control.

TASK:
1. Read /gin/context.go and find `FileAttachment` (and any related helper such as `File`, `FileFromFS`, or a quote-escaping helper). Confirm the root cause: the filename is interpolated into the `Content-Disposition` header without escaping `"` and `\`.
2. Determine the correct, in-repo-evidenced behavior. Look for: doc comments on FileAttachment, README/CHANGELOG mentions, and pre-existing tests in /gin/context_test.go (search for FileAttachment / Content-Disposition) which show the exact expected header string. IMPORTANT: the fix must keep the existing tested output for normal filenames byte-for-byte identical (e.g. `attachment; filename="report.pdf"`).
3. IMPORTANT: before editing, record the baseline: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`. Then check whether any pre-existing test asserts the current (unescaped) behavior for a filename containing quotes/backslashes. If a pre-existing test asserts the buggy behavior, DO NOT change that test; report the conflict to me instead.
4. Apply the minimal fix so that `"` and `\` in the filename are escaped (e.g. backslash-escaped) when building the Content-Disposition header, so the header contains exactly one well-formed filename parameter. Keep it minimal and idiomatic; do not restructure the function or change behavior for ordinary filenames.
5. Verify with a temporary standalone program OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/repro6 with a go.mod using `replace github.com/gin-gonic/gin => /gin`, GOFLAGS=-mod=mod GOPROXY=off GOSUMDB=off) using net/http/httptest: call FileAttachment with a normal filename (expect unchanged `attachment; filename="report.pdf"`) and with the malicious filename (expect the quotes/backslashes escaped so there is exactly one filename parameter, e.g. `attachment; filename="evil\"; dummy=\"x.sh"` with proper backslash escaping). Parse the resulting header with a proper header parser if useful to demonstrate it now yields a single parameter. Clean up /tmp files; leave no stray files in /gin.
6. Run `cd /gin && gofmt -l . && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...`. Confirm no pre-existing test regresses (compare with baseline; `git stash` of your change can double-check).

BUG REPORT (from a user):
I'm registering routes at runtime, after the server has already handled a request. If I send a request for a path that isn't registered yet I get a 404, which is fine, but once I register the matching route with parameters and send the same request again, the handler runs and returns 200 while every URL parameter comes back empty — c.Param("name") is "", c.Params.ByName("last_name") is "", and c.Params.Get("wild") returns "" and false.

    // first request, before the route exists -> 404
    GET /test/john/smith/is/super/great

    router.GET("/test/:name/:last_name/*wild", func(c *gin.Context) {
        c.Param("name") // "" — I expected "john"
    })

    // same request again -> 200, but all params are empty
    GET /test/john/smith/is/super/great

I expect the parameters to be populated exactly as they are when the route is registered before the first request.

LIKELY CAUSE (verify it yourself, do not assume): /gin/tree.go keeps a per-method skip cache (the `skips` type, `tskips` field in methodTree, used by `getValue`) that records paths which did not match. When a route is added later via `addRoute`, this cache is not invalidated, so the previously-missed path is short-circuited and the handler is invoked without walking the tree, leaving Params empty. Confirm by reading /gin/tree.go (getValue, addRoute, the skips/tskips logic) and /gin/gin.go (addRoute / handleHTTPRequest).

Apply the minimal fix so that a route added after a miss is found correctly with populated params (e.g. reset/clear the skip cache when a route is added, or make the cache only apply when the tree is unchanged). BUG REPORT (from a user):
When a client sends an `Accept` header that starts with one of the formats I offer but has extra characters at the end, my server crashes instead of just not matching.

    c.Request.Header.Set("Accept", "image/tiff-fx")
    format := c.NegotiateFormat("image/tiff")

I expected NegotiateFormat to return an empty string, since `image/tiff-fx` is not the same as `image/tiff`. Instead the request panicked with `runtime error: index out of range [10] with length 10`.

LIKELY CAUSE (verify it yourself, do not assume): /gin/context.go's `NegotiateFormat` (and/or the `accepted`/`Accept` handling) does a prefix/suffix comparison that slices the accepted value using the length of the offered format without checking the accepted string is long enough — e.g. something like `accepted[i:i+len(offer)] == offer` or `accepted[:len(offer)]`. When the accepted string is shorter than the offer, that slice is out of range. Confirm by reading /gin/context.go (NegotiateFormat) and any helpers.

Also test the reverse ordering (offer longer than accepted) and other lengths to pin down the exact off-by-one/out-of-range condition.
2. Read /gin/context.go's NegotiateFormat and related code; determine the precise root cause and the correct matching semantics. Look for in-repo evidence of the intended behavior: the doc comment on NegotiateFormat, README, and the pre-existing tests in /gin/context_test.go (e.g. TestContextNegotiationFormat, TestContextNegotiationFormatWithAccept) — these show exactly what matching is expected (e.g. how "text/html" vs "text/html; charset=utf-8" vs "application/xml" are handled).

A panic in request handling is also a universally-accepted violation.
5. Verify: rerun the repro — NegotiateFormat("image/tiff") with Accept "image/tiff-fx" must return "" with no panic; also check Accept "image/tiff;q=0.5", "image/*", "*/*", "text/html,application/xml", and the multi-offer forms used in the existing tests. BUG REPORT (from a user):
I set up my router with `RedirectFixedPath = true` and registered a static route and a parameter route under the same prefix. When I request the path with different casing or with extra segments, the server panics with `invalid node type` instead of redirecting to the static route or returning a 404. I expected `/PREFIX/XXX` to redirect to `/prefix/xxx`, and `/prefix/a/b/c` to simply 404.

    r.RedirectFixedPath = true
    r.GET("/prefix/:id", handler)
    r.GET("/prefix/xxx", handler)
    // request /PREFIX/XXX or /prefix/a/b/c -> panic: invalid node type
